(a) 
There is authorized to be appropriated $1,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1967, which shall be available only for the purpose of preparing the report provided for in subsection (b) of this section. There are authorized to be appropriated $40,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968, and $90,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this title. For the fiscal years thereafter there shall be appropriated for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this title only such amounts as he Congress may hereafter authorize by law.
 
    (b) The Secretary shall prepare, with the advice of the Advisory Committee appointed pursuant to section 106, a report containing specific recommendations for carrying out the provisions of this title, including any recommendations for amendments to this title and to portions of other laws amended by this Act, and shall submit such report to the President and the Congress not later than April 30, 1967.
 
    (c) Prior to January 31, 1968, and prior to January 31 in each year thereafter, the Secretary shall make a report to the Congress which reviews and evaluates activities carried on under the authority of this Act and which reviews other activities of the Federal Government drawing upon or strengthening American resources for international study and research and any existing activities and plans to coordinate and improve the efforts of the Federal Government in international education.

fable.w: The Secretary must obtain the advice of an Advisory Committee when formulating specific recommendations on how to carry out the title, which brings an advisory body into a federal policy determination. The tempting "No" reading is that this is only a report to Congress and the President, which stays inside the government, and that advice on a report is not advice on a decision. That reading is weakened because the report sets implementation recommendations rather than merely presenting a study, and advisory committees of this kind typically include non-federal members, although this section does not itself state the committee's membership.
fable.s: The Secretary shall prepare, with the advice of the Advisory Committee appointed pursuant to section 106, a report containing specific recommendations for carrying out the provisions of this title

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to prepare a report containing specific recommendations for carrying out the title's provisions, and explicitly mandates doing so 'with the advice of the Advisory Committee.' Advisory committees are typically composed of outside experts or stakeholders, and their advice constitutes participation in the decision-making process before the final report is submitted. This fits the definition of participation via an advisory body.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall prepare, with the advice of the Advisory Committee appointed pursuant to section 106, a report containing specific recommendations for carrying out the provisions of this title

opus.w: The Secretary must get advice from an Advisory Committee before writing recommendations on how to run the program and how to amend the law. That is advisory-committee input into a federal policy decision, like the advisory bodies in Examples 10 and 12. One could read this as only a report to Congress, or as outside input on a study (Example 3). But the committee shapes the Secretary's own program recommendations, and such committees are typically made up of outside experts. Membership is not shown in this section, so that last point is an assumption.
opus.s: The Secretary shall prepare, with the advice of the Advisory Committee appointed pursuant to section 106, a report containing specific recommendations for carrying out the provisions of this title, including any recommendations for amendments to this title

I labelled this **Yes**, with moderate confidence (0.66). An advisory committee helps shape the Secretary's recommendations, though the Advisory Committee's membership isn't shown in this text.

1. **The tempting reading.** Subsections (b) and (c) are mostly about reports to the President and Congress, which stay inside the federal government. Example 3 also treats outside input on the contents of a study as not participation. On that view, the committee is just helping write a report.
2. **Why it fails here.** Subsection (b) requires the Secretary to prepare the report "with the advice of the Advisory Committee appointed pursuant to section 106." The report is not a fact-finding study. It holds the Secretary's recommendations for running the program, including proposed changes to the law. Like the advisory bodies in Examples 10 and 12, the committee helps shape a federal decision.
3. **The uncertainty.** The committee's members aren't listed in this section. My view that they are outside education experts comes from what I recall of the 1966 International Education Act, not from the text. If they turned out to be federal officials, the answer would be No.
